title: Bobbie T Experience 6887 NDE 6887
content: I was admitted to the hospital to try and stop labor when I was thirty four to thirty five weeks pregnant with twins. After nineteen hours, an emergency Cesarean Section was performed due to distress of one baby. The anesthesiologist gave me medication to put me to sleep and I did go to sleep, sort of. It was odd. I couldn't move or respond, so I appeared to be out but I could see and hear and feel everything. I felt them strap my arms down and intubate me. Then the doctor started to cut open my abdomen, and the pain was unbearable. I started yelling in my head at the doctor to stop and I was screaming at them, but they couldn't hear me. The doctor asked the anesthesiologist if I was out enough and he zapped me in the left temple with some type of electrical ‘gun’. I yelled at him to stop that, that it hurt. The pain just went on and on, I was panicking. I felt the doctor pull both babies out and my body pulled up off the table with each baby. The babies both peed and the doctors and nurses laughed. I remember thinking that I shouldn't be able to feel all this, let alone hear and see the people in the room. The next thing I remember was turning my head to the right, but I knew that was impossible since my head was strapped down. To my right was the most beautiful white soft glowing light. At this point, I no longer felt any pain, although I could still hear what was going on in the room. I felt as if I was going to the light and I was very happy and pain free. I heard one of the babies cry and I quickly turned my head and could see the room as if from far away, just then a male voice, over my right shoulder, said to me, ‘It's not time yet, go back.’ It was a beautiful, kind and loving voice. Next thing I knew I had literally slammed into my body with such force and the pain started all over again. They must have given me more anesthesia as I went out completely shortly after returning.

out_of_body.vantage_other_detail: She reports being unable to move/respond while still able to see/hear/feel the surgery, then later says she could see the room 'as if from far away' and also describes turning her head despite it being strapped down.
out_of_body.separation_sensations_other: Panicking during unbearable pain; later happy and pain-free while drawn to the light.

arrival.other_being_detail: A male voice over her right shoulder told her, 'It's not time yet, go back.'

environment.environment_other_detail: Described as 'the most beautiful white soft glowing light.'

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Emergency Cesarean section under anesthesia at 34-35 weeks pregnant with twins.

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Auditory awareness of operating room continued during the light encounter; return described as slamming back into body with pain resuming.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Awareness of the operating room and body sensations precede a light encounter; brief 'not your time' message and immediate return.
stage_sequence.simultaneous_stage_detail: While seeing/being drawn to the light, she could still hear what was going on in the operating room.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Experience occurred during anesthesia with paralysis/awareness and severe pain; she reports an electrical 'gun' to the left temple and continued hearing the operating room while drawn to a soft white light.
